question: The AI Act1 aims to ensure that AI technologies are safe, ethical and transparent, while also fostering innovation to support economic and social progress within the EU. To achieve these objectives, the AI Act must provide legal certainty and foster trust. A key element in this regard is a clear definition of what constitutes an AI system.

Recital 12 of the AI Act requires that this definition be aligned with international standards. The Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD) has noted that AI systems are developed using machine learning or logic- or knowledge-based approaches, excluding simple statistical techniques such as linear or logistic regression.

Recital 12 also highlights that a key characteristic of an AI system is its capacity to infer, which must go beyond basic data processing by enabling learning, reasoning or modelling. Article 96(1)(f) of the AI Act mandates the Commission to develop guidelines for the practical implementation of the definition of AI systems. In this context: 1.
How will the Commission ensure that the definition of AI systems in the EU aligns with the OECD definition (therefore excluding simple statistical techniques)?
Will the Commission explain in its upcoming guidelines the meaning of ‘basic data processing’ in relation to an AI system’s capacity to infer?

Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 13 June 2024 laying down harmonised rules on artificial intelligence and amending Regulations (EC) No 300/2008, (EU) No 167/2013, (EU) No 168/2013, (EU) 2018/858, (EU) 2018/1139 and (EU) 2019/2144 and Directives 2014/90/EU, (EU) 2016/797 and (EU) 2020/1828 (Artificial Intelligence Act) (OJ L, 2024/1689, 12.7.2024, ELI: http://data.europa.eu/eli/reg/2024/1689/oj).
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (7.3.2025) The Artificial Intelligence Act (the AI Act)1 defines an AI system in its Article 3(1). This definition is already aligned to the definition of ‘AI system’ included in the 2024 revised Recommendation of the Council on Artificial Intelligence of the Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD)2.

In line with Article 96 (1)(f) AI Act, the Commission developed guidelines on the application of the definition of ‘AI system’ used in the AI Act3. These guidelines explain that neither Article 3(1) AI Act, nor recital 12 AI Act which clarifies that provision, explicitly excludes statistical methods from the scope of the definition of ‘AI system’.

Recital 12 clarifies that ‘the definition should be based on key characteristics of AI systems that distinguish it from simpler traditional software systems or programming approaches and should not cover systems that are based on the rules defined solely by natural persons to automatically execute operations’. Recital 12 further states that ‘[a] key characteristic of AI systems is their capability to infer.

The capacity of an AI system to infer transcends basic data processing by enabling learning, reasoning or modelling’. In the guidelines, systems for improving mathematical optimisation, basic data processing systems, systems based on classical heuristics and simple prediction systems, are considered outside the scope of the AI system definition.
1 Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 13 June 2024 laying down

harmonised rules on artificial intelligence and amending Regulations (EC) No 300/2008, (EU) No 167/2013, (EU) No 168/2013, (EU) 2018/858, (EU) 2018/1139 and (EU) 2019/2144 and Directives 2014/90/EU, (EU) 2016/797 and (EU) 2020/1828. 2 OECD, Recommendation of the Council on Artificial Intelligence, OECD/LEGAL/0449. 3 https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/library/commission-publishes-guidelines-ai-system-definition-facilitatefirst-ai-acts-rules-application
